content: Phenylephrine, pramoxine, glycerin, and petrolatum should be applied to a cleansed area either externally or to the lower portion of the anal canal. This medication can be used up to four times daily, particularly at night, in the morning, or after bowel movements that may aggravate hemorrhoids. For application to the lower anal canal, remove the cover from the dispensing cap and attach the cap to the tube. For intrarectal use, remove the cover from the applicator, attach the applicator to the ointment tube, lubricate the applicator thoroughly, and gently insert it into the rectum. After each use, clean the applicator and replace the cover. For children under 12 years of age, use is determined based on the patient’s condition and whether the benefits outweigh the risks. For individuals aged 12 years or older, the medication should be applied to a cleansed area externally or to the lower anal canal, up to four times daily, especially at night, in the morning, or after bowel movements that may worsen hemorrhoids. This product is for external use only. It should be kept out of the reach of children. Discontinue use and consult a physician if hemorrhoids worsen or do not improve within seven days. Additionally, stop use if symptoms such as bleeding, allergic reactions, redness, irritation, swelling, pain, or other adverse effects develop or worsen. Do not exceed the recommended daily dosage unless directed by a healthcare professional. Avoid inserting the medication into the rectum using fingers, mechanical devices, or applicators unless specifically instructed by a healthcare provider. This medication is generally considered safe during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. However, it is always advisable to consult a healthcare professional before use.
